learningObjective: Contrast CPU SIMD lane execution with GPU SIMT warp execution, identifying differences in divergence handling, thread identity and programming model.

canonicalClaims.claim: SIMT (NVIDIA GPUs) exposes lane-level threads with independent logical state and manages branch divergence in hardware, while SIMD (CPU vector ISAs like AVX-512) exposes lanes as packed vector operands manipulated by explicit instructions and typically requires software-generated predication/masking for divergent control.
conditions: GPU baseline is Volta+ (independent thread scheduling).
CPU baseline is a wide-vector ISA such as AVX-512.
nonImplications: Does not imply that SIMT eliminates divergence overhead; taken/not-taken paths still serialize.
Does not imply CPU SIMD lacks masking support; modern ISAs have mask registers.

misconceptions.claim: SIMT and SIMD are identical models under different names.
misconceptions.whyWrong: They differ in programming abstraction (threads vs lanes), divergence handling (hardware vs software), and thread-identity semantics.

misconceptions.claim: SIMT wastes silicon area vs SIMD by a fixed ~30%.
misconceptions.whyWrong: No such universal figure exists; efficiency comparisons depend on workload, precision, memory system and target ISA.

misconceptions.claim: SIMD ISAs cannot handle divergent branches at all.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Predication and mask-registers are standard tools in modern SIMD ISAs; the difference is that divergence handling is explicit rather than hardware-managed.

misconceptions.claim: Post-Volta warps behave lockstep with a single shared PC.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Since Volta, threads within a warp have independent PCs and support reconvergence; the pre-Volta lockstep model is outdated for correctness reasoning.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: CUDA C++ Programming Guide, Volta independent thread scheduling

implementationFacts: Warp size on NVIDIA GPUs = 32; warp threads share a scheduler but have independent state.
AVX-512 exposes 8 mask registers (k0..k7) for lane predication.
performanceScenarios: Kernels with unpredictable data-dependent branches see divergence costs on GPUs and must vectorize carefully on CPUs; both models converge in cost when divergence is high.
